dedupe_keys.name: inferring gerd reservoir filling strategies with hydrological modelling and earth observation hess 2023

description: This case study is a HESS paper that develops a framework to work out how the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam was being filled when the operator shares no information, so downstream managers in Sudan can adjust their own dam operation. Five rainfall products were compared with ten rain stations; the three best drove the conceptual HBV-light model with ERA5 evapotranspiration and temperature, calibrated for 2006 to 2019 and validated for 1991 to 1996; good parameter sets predicted GERD inflow for 2020 to 2022; and daily storage from the water balance was checked against Landsat and Sentinel storage estimates. The best run, using CHIRPS, matched with root mean square errors of 1.7 and 1.52 billion cubic metres and NSE of 0.77 and 0.86. GERD held 14 percent of July 2020 inflow, 41 percent of July 2021 and 37 and 32 percent in July and August 2022, and 5.2 and 7.4 percent of annual inflow in the first two phases and 12.9 to 13.7 percent in the third. Coverage: the Blue Nile upstream of Sudan, 2020 to 2022. Access: free article under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: the result is a retrieval from models, not observed releases, and rainfall input uncertainty dominates. It informs transboundary reservoir monitoring and downstream operation simulation, and relates to the CHIRPS rainfall record already in the catalogue.

name: Inferring GERD reservoir filling strategies with hydrological modelling and Earth observation (HESS 2023)
outcomes: Retrieved three years of filling: the dam stored 14 percent of July 2020 inflow, 41 percent in July 2021 and 37 and 32 percent in July and August 2022, and about 5.2 to 13.7 percent of annual inflow by phase, with input uncertainty mattering more than parameter uncertainty.
